mainTopic: שירים, כיבוס and מחשבה according to רבי נחמיה; reading 'from the corner' and 'from the base'; why every placement of the inner offerings is essential
overview: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with three laws for blood poured on the יסוד: it requires כיבוס, מחשבה works on it, and offering it outside makes one liable. Drain blood gets the opposite three laws. Since only רבי נחמיה holds that offering שירים outside makes one liable, the ברייתא is his, and so he requires כיבוס for שירים. The גמרא challenges this, because another ברייתא says מחשבה does not work on שירים. It first suggests the ברייתא means the blood of the last three placements of a חטאת, but rejects that, since those placements are treated like שירים. It then settles on the שירים of the inner offerings, and explains through רבי נחמיה's view why the ברייתא contrasted them with drain blood. Next, רבינא defends רב פפא by reading the משנה's 'from the corner' literally and 'from the base' as blood fit for the base, and he rejects רב תחליפא בר גזא's challenge. Finally, the גמרא turns to the משנה about blood placed on the inner מזבח. A ברייתא learns from ויקרא 4:20 that every placement is essential, and it begins to read the word 'לפר' as pointing to the פר יום הכפורים, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא: blood for the altar's base versus blood for the drain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא contrasting blood that goes on the יסוד with blood poured into the drain, across three laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught in a ברייתא: Blood that must be poured on the base of the altar requires laundering, improper intent works on it, and someone who offers it outside the Temple is liable. Blood that is poured into the drain does not require laundering, improper intent does not work on it, and someone who offers it outside is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as support. It sets up a clear contrast between two kinds of blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood that goes on the יסוד is the leftover blood (שירים) of a חטאת. The ברייתא treats it as real altar blood in three ways: כיבוס, מחשבה, and liability for offering it outside. Blood thrown into the drain is just waste, so none of these three laws apply to it.

keyTerms.meaning: The base of the altar, where the leftover blood is poured
Laundering a garment that blood splashed on
Improper intent 'works', meaning it can disqualify the offering (for example, make it פיגול)
Someone who offers a sacrifice outside the Temple
The drain channel in the Temple courtyard

steps.confusionAlert: Here וְהָתַנְיָא introduces support for the previous point. It is not an attack, even though the same word is often used to challenge.

phrases.english: And so it is taught: blood that requires the base of the altar
requires laundering,
and improper intent is effective with it,
and one who offers it up outside is liable;
and blood that is poured into the drain
does not require laundering,
and improper intent is not effective with it,
and one who offers it up outside is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support the earlier discussion about whether שירים require כיבוס
steps.raayaObject: That the leftover blood poured on the יסוד requires כיבוס
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא contrasting blood for the יסוד with blood for the drain

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי נחמיה, so he requires laundering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא identifies the author of the ברייתא as רבי נחמיה, which shows that he holds שירים require כיבוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who have you heard say that someone who offers this blood outside is liable? That is רבי נחמיה. And in this ברייתא he says it requires laundering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof by showing whose opinion the ברייתא follows. Since it must be רבי נחמיה, we learn his view on כיבוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only רבי נחמיה holds that offering the שירים outside makes a person liable. The ברייתא says exactly that, so it must be his. The same ברייתא also says this blood requires כיבוס, so רבי נחמיה must hold that too.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Who have you heard say...?', a way of identifying the author of a teaching

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא matches רבי נחמיה, and it shows that he requires כיבוס for the leftover blood.

phrases.english: Whom have you heard who says
one who offers them up outside is liable?
It is רבי נחמיה;
and he says: it requires laundering.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן שָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ דְּאָמַר מַעֲלֶה מֵהֶן בַּחוּץ חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the author of the ברייתא from step 1 to complete the proof
steps.raayaObject: רבי נחמיה's view that שירים require כיבוס
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's ruling that offering them outside makes one liable, which only רבי נחמיה holds

steps.title: Does improper intent really work on the leftover blood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's claim that מחשבה works on שירים, citing another ברייתא that says it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does improper intent really work on this blood? But it is taught in another ברייתא: the leftover blood and the burning of the sacrificial parts are excluded, because they do not hold back atonement, so improper intent does not work on them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks one detail of the ברייתא it just used. Another ברייתא says מחשבה has no effect on שירים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מחשבה (such as פיגול) only works on a service that the כפרה depends on. Pouring the שירים and burning the אימורין are not required for כפרה, so the second ברייתא says מחשבה does not work on them. That directly contradicts the first ברייתא's claim.

keyTerms.meaning: The leftover blood poured on the יסוד after the main sprinklings
Burning the sacrificial fats and parts on the altar
Hold back; required, so that without them it does not work
Atonement achieved by the offering

phrases.english: And is improper intent effective with them?!
But isn't it taught: excluded are the leftover blood
and the burning of the sacrificial parts,
which do not hold back the atonement
so improper intent is not effective with them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the מחשבה clause of the ברייתא quoted in step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that מחשבה works on blood poured on the יסוד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא says מחשבה works only on services the כפרה depends on. שירים are not such a service, so מחשבה should not work on them.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about the last three placements of a חטאת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is not talking about the leftover blood. It is talking about the blood of the last three מתנות of a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: When that ברייתא was taught, it was about the three placements of the חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 3. It moves the ברייתא off the leftover blood and onto the blood of the later placements of a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 asked how מחשבה could work on שירים when another ברייתא says it does not. The answer is that our ברייתא was never about true שירים. It was about the blood used for the three placements after the first one, so the two ברייתות no longer clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Placements of blood on the מזבח
Sin offering
The three placements of a חטאת that come after the first one

phrases.english: When that [ברייתא] was taught –
phrases.notes: 'That ברייתא' is the one from Step 1, about blood that goes on the יסוד.

phrases.english: it was about the three placements of the sin offering.
phrases.notes: A חטאת gets four placements, one on each corner. These are the three that come after the first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 3 by giving the ברייתא a different subject.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the case the ברייתא refers to
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was about the leftover blood (שירים), which does not work with מחשבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about the blood of the last three מתנות of a חטאת.

steps.title: That blood goes to the corner, not to the base
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the answer. The blood of the three מתנות goes on the corners (קרנות) of the מזבח, so how can the ברייתא call it blood that requires the יסוד?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, how can it say they 'require the base'? They go to the corner!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 4. The wording of the ברייתא does not fit the blood of the three placements.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא describes the blood as 'טעונין יסוד', blood that needs the base. But the three מתנות are placed on a קרן, a corner of the מזבח, not on the יסוד. So the ברייתא's own wording seems to rule out Step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: Requiring the base of the מזבח
A corner of the מזבח
If so

phrases.english: If so, [can it say they] require the base?!
They go to the corner!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 4's answer using the ברייתא's wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in Step 4 that the ברייתא refers to the three מתנות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The three מתנות are placed on a קרן, so they cannot be called blood that requires the יסוד.

steps.title: Read it as blood that will later need the base
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the reading to 'ניטענין יסוד', meaning blood that will end up needing the יסוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: they 'become required' for the base.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends Step 4 by slightly changing how we read the words of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new reading does not mean the blood goes to the יסוד right now. It means that whatever is left of it at the end will be poured on the יסוד. That way the wording fits blood that first goes to the corner.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead (read it this way)
Will become required for the base

phrases.english: Say [instead]: they become required for the base.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 5's wording challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'טעונין יסוד' means the blood itself goes to the יסוד.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means blood that will eventually be poured on the יסוד.

steps.title: מחשבה does not work on the three placements either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks again. We were taught that the three מתנות are treated like the end blood: they do not permit the meat, do not make פיגול, and are not affected by being brought inside. So how can מחשבה work on them?
steps.simpleTranslation: And does improper intent work on them? Didn't you say they don't permit, don't make פיגול, and aren't affected by entering inside, just like the end blood?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, stronger challenge to Step 4. Even with the new reading, the three placements still do not fit what the ברייתא says about מחשבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earlier teaching said the last three מתנות act like the leftover blood ('כסופן') in every way: they are not מתיר, cannot make פיגול, and entering the היכל does not disqualify them. If they are like שירים, the same problem from Step 3 comes back, because מחשבה would not work on them.

keyTerms.meaning: Improper intent during the עבודה
Permits the offering to be eaten or offered
Makes the offering פיגול
Like their end, meaning like the leftover blood

phrases.english: And is improper intent effective with them?!
Didn't you say: they do not permit, and do not make פיגול,
and entering inside [does not disqualify] – [they are] like their end!
phrases.notes: 'Inside' means into the היכל. Normally חטאת blood brought in there makes the offering פסול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second attack on Step 4, this time on the law and not the wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא, which says מחשבה works, refers to the three מתנות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The three מתנות are treated like שירים in every way, so מחשבה should not work on them.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about the leftover blood of inner offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the three-placements answer. It says the ברייתא is about the שירים after all, but only the שירים of offerings whose blood is sprinkled inside (דמים הפנימיים).
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, when that ברייתא was taught, it was about the inner blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on Step 4 and offers a new answer. The ברייתא is about leftover blood, but only from the inner חטאות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the ברייתא really is talking about שירים poured on the יסוד, so the wording fits. Limiting it to inner offerings is meant to explain why מחשבה works on these שירים. The other ברייתא, which says מחשבה does not work on שירים, would then be about outer offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood of offerings sprinkled inside, on the inner מזבח
Rather (drops the earlier answer)

phrases.english: Rather, when that [ברייתא] was taught –
it was about the inner blood.
phrases.notes: He means the leftover blood of the inner offerings, which is poured on the יסוד of the outer מזבח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Abandons Step 4 after Step 7 and answers Step 3 a new way.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ברייתא to a narrower case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about the three מתנות of a חטאת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about the שירים of the inner offerings.

steps.title: Then the ברייתא should have contrasted inner and outer blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new answer. If outer שירים would be פטור, why did the ברייתא contrast with blood poured into the drain? It should have drawn the line inside the case of שירים itself: inner is חייב, outer is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: But with outer blood, what is the law, פטור? Then instead of teaching about blood poured into the drain, let it make the distinction within its own case: When is this said? With inner blood. But with outer blood, one is exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 8. The way the ברייתא is built does not fit an inner-only reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא meant only inner שירים, it implies that outer שירים are פטור. In that case the natural contrast was right there: inner versus outer שירים. Choosing to contrast with drain blood instead suggests the ברייתא was not limited to inner offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood of offerings sprinkled on the outer מזבח
Exempt
Instead of teaching
Let it make a distinction within its own case
The drain channel in the עזרה

steps.whatToRemember: The challenge rests on the ברייתא's choice to contrast its blood with drain blood rather than with outer שירים. The next step answers it.

phrases.english: But with outer blood, what [is the law]? Exempt?!
phrases.notes: He means someone who offers that leftover blood outside the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: Instead of teaching about blood poured into the drain;
let it distinguish and teach within its own [case]:
In what [case] are these words said?
With inner blood,
but with outer blood – exempt!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 8's inner-only reading based on how the ברייתא is structured.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in Step 8 that the ברייתא refers only to inner שירים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If outer שירים are פטור, the ברייתא should have contrasted inner and outer שירים, not שירים and drain blood.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי נחמיה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא follows רבי נחמיה, who holds that outer שירים offered outside also make one חייב. So it could not set inner שירים against outer שירים and still list three exemptions next to three liabilities.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this ברייתא? It is רבי נחמיה, who says that if someone offers the leftover blood outside, he is liable. So if the ברייתא had contrasted inner and outer שירים, it could not have taught three exemptions alongside three liabilities.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 9. It explains why the ברייתא compared inner שירים to blood poured into the drain instead of to outer שירים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that outer שירים offered outside are פטור, so the ברייתא should have drawn its line inside שירים. But according to רבי נחמיה, outer שירים offered outside are also חייב. That means there is no 'exempt' side among שירים, so the ברייתא had to bring a different exempt case, the blood poured into the drain, to set three exemptions next to three liabilities.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is this? A way of naming the author of a teaching
The leftover blood that remains after the required placements
Outside the בית המקדש
Exemptions / liabilities

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא follows רבי נחמיה. In his view, even outer שירים offered outside make one חייב, so the ברייתא's 'exempt' examples had to come from somewhere else.

phrases.english: Whose view is this? It is רבי נחמיה,
who says: the leftover blood
that one offered outside, he is liable;
phrases.notes: He means even the leftover blood of offerings whose blood goes on the outer מזבח.

phrases.english: and so he could not teach it
as three exemptions alongside three liabilities.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the author of the ברייתא, whose view removes the expected contrast
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Outer שירים offered outside are פטור, so the ברייתא should have contrasted inner and outer שירים
steps.terutzMaskana: Under רבי נחמיה, outer שירים offered outside are also חייב, so the exempt side had to come from blood poured into the drain

steps.title: רבינא's reading: 'from the corner' literally, 'from the base' means fit for the base
steps.stepSummary: רבינא goes back to רב פפא's rule and defends it. He reads the משנה's 'from the corner' literally, and 'from the base' as blood that is fit for the base.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא says: 'From the corner' means literally from the corner. 'From the base' means from blood that is fit for the base.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the earlier discussion of רב פפא, who said that a garment sprayed with blood meant for the last three placements needs washing. רבינא offers a new way to read the משנה so that it supports רב פפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that blood sprayed 'from the corner' or 'from the base' does not need washing. רבינא says 'from the corner' means blood already placed on the corner. So blood that is only fit for the corner and not yet placed, like the blood for the last three placements, still needs washing, just as רב פפא said. 'From the base', on the other hand, he reads as the שירים, which are fit to be poured on the base.

keyTerms.meaning: A corner of the מזבח
The base of the מזבח, where the leftover blood is poured
Literally, actually
What is fit or meant for something

steps.confusionAlert: The two halves of the line are read in different ways. 'From the corner' is literal (already placed), but 'from the base' means only 'fit for the base' (not yet poured).

phrases.english: רבינא says:
'from the corner' means literally from the corner,
phrases.notes: He is reading the words of the משנה about blood that sprayed onto a garment.

phrases.english: 'from the base' means from blood that is fit for the base.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the earlier objection against רב פפא and offers a new answer
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reads the two terms in the משנה in two different ways
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה shows that blood fit for the corner does not need washing, which goes against רב פפא
steps.terutzMaskana: Only blood already on the corner is exempt from washing; blood only fit for the corner still needs washing

steps.title: רב תחליפא בר גזא: maybe both mean 'fit for'
steps.stepSummary: רב תחליפא בר גזא challenges רבינא. Why not read both terms as 'fit for'? Then blood fit for the corner would not need washing, against רב פפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב תחליפא בר גזא said to רבינא: Say that both this one and that one mean blood that is fit for it!
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא challenges רבינא's split reading. He suggests reading 'from the corner' as 'fit for the corner,' just like 'from the base.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both terms mean 'fit for,' then blood that is only fit for the corner would also not need washing. That would knock down רב פפא's rule again. So the challenge reopens the problem רבינא just solved.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who challenges רבינא
Say instead, I could argue
Both this and that

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב תַּחְלִיפָא בַּר גַּזָּא לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: רב תחליפא בר גזא said to רבינא:
Say that both this and that mean blood that is fit for it!
phrases.notes: Meaning: 'from the corner' would also mean only 'fit for the corner,' not yet placed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבינא's reading from step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's split reading of 'from the corner' and 'from the base'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two terms could be read the same way, and then the משנה would go against רב פפא

steps.title: רבינא: then 'from the base' would be pointless
steps.stepSummary: רבינא rejects the challenge. If blood fit for the corner does not need washing, there would be no need to say so about blood fit for the base.
steps.simpleTranslation: What kind of argument is this? Now, if blood fit for the corner does not need washing, as you say, do we even need to be told about blood fit for the base?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא pushes back against רב תחליפא בר גזא. He shows that his reading would make part of the משנה unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood for the corner is the more important blood, and the blood for the base is only the leftover. If even the corner blood does not need washing, then of course the leftover blood would not need it either. A משנה does not say something so obvious, so the two terms cannot both mean 'fit for.'

keyTerms.meaning: What is this? A way of rejecting an argument as weak
Now, if (opening an 'all the more so' argument)
Is it even necessary to say?

phrases.english: What is this argument?
Now, blood fit for the corner, you said does not need washing;
is it even necessary to say this about blood fit for the base?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי מַאי? הַשְׁתָּא רָאוּי לַקֶּרֶן – אָמְרַתְּ לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that both terms mean 'fit for'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would make the words 'from the base' unnecessary, since that case would follow automatically

steps.title: Conclusion: the corner is literal, the base means fit for the base
steps.stepSummary: רבינא's reading stands: 'from the corner' means actually from the corner, and 'from the base' means blood fit for the base.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, 'from the corner' means literally from the corner, and 'from the base' means from blood that is fit for the base.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא repeats his reading as the final conclusion of this discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the 'both mean fit for' reading would make the משנה say something obvious, the only sensible reading is the split one. This keeps רב פפא's rule that blood fit for the corner, but not yet placed, still needs washing.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, so it must be

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה is read as: 'from the corner' means already on the corner, and 'from the base' means the שירים fit for the base. This keeps רב פפא's rule in place.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מִן הַקֶּרֶן – מִן הַקֶּרֶן מַמָּשׁ,
phrases.english: Rather, 'from the corner' means from the corner, literally,
'from the base' means from blood that is fit for the base.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִן הַקֶּרֶן – מִן הַקֶּרֶן מַמָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates רבינא's reading after rejecting the challenge
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבינא's reading stands, and רב פפא's rule about washing a garment is upheld

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about blood placed on the inner מזבח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the opening words of the משנה about offerings whose blood is placed on the inner מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'All the offerings whose blood is placed on the inner מזבח...' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה. This sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that for blood placed on the inner מזבח, if even one placement is missed, the offering does not bring atonement. The גמרא now begins to look for where this comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: The inner (golden) מזבח inside the היכל
Those whose blood is placed
Etc.; the quote continues

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַנִּיתָּנִין עַל מִזְבֵּחַ הַפְּנִימִי כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: All those whose blood is placed on the inner מזבח, etc.
phrases.notes: This is the start of the משנה's line; it goes on to say that missing even one placement means no atonement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For offerings whose blood goes on the inner מזבח, every placement is required

steps.title: What does 'ועשה כאשר עשה' come to teach?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks what the פסוק 'ועשה כאשר עשה' adds about the פר העלם דבר של ציבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'And he shall do as he did.' What does this come to teach?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that opens with a question about a פסוק. This sets up the explanation that will follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק compares the communal bull to the bull of the כהן משיח. Many details already seem to be written out for the communal bull too. So the ברייתא asks what this comparison adds that we would not already know.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he shall do as he did,' the פסוק comparing the two bulls
What does it come to teach?

phrases.english: The רבנן taught:
'And he shall do as he did':
what does it come to teach?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: וְעָשָׂה כַּאֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה – מָה בָּא לִלְמוֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the search for the source of the משנה just quoted
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the extra comparison in 'ועשה כאשר עשה' adds

steps.title: The repeated verse makes every placement essential
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers that the פסוק repeats the sprinkling to teach that leaving out even one placement makes the whole service worthless.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse repeats the sprinkling. This teaches that if the כהן left out even one of the placements, he has done nothing at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question from step 16: the extra words are there to repeat the law of sprinkling the blood. Because it is said twice, it teaches that missing even one placement ruins everything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the תורה says something twice, it shows the detail is essential and not just a recommendation. So each single sprinkling of the פר העלם דבר is required. One missing placement means the כהן 'did nothing'.

keyTerms.meaning: to double, to say twice
sprinkling of the blood
placements of blood
he has done nothing at all; the service does not count

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule for the inner offerings: each blood placement is essential. The rest of the derivation builds on it.

phrases.english: to repeat [the law of] its sprinkling;
phrases.notes: This answers step 16's question: the extra words 'ועשה כאשר עשה' are there to say the sprinkling a second time.

phrases.english: and this teaches that if he left out
one of all the placements –
he has done nothing at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16 about what 'ועשה כאשר עשה' adds.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse repeats the sprinkling, which makes every single placement essential.

steps.title: What about the four placements on the inner altar?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says it has proven the rule only for the seven sprinklings, and asks where we learn it for the four placements.
steps.simpleTranslation: I only know this about the seven placements, which are essential in every case. How do I know it about the four placements?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא limits what it just proved. It says the lesson clearly covers the seven sprinklings, and asks how we know the four placements on the inner מזבח are also essential.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seven sprinklings are essential 'everywhere', so it is easy to apply the rule to them. The four placements are not described that way, so we might have thought missing one is not fatal. The ברייתא needs a separate source for them.

keyTerms.meaning: I only know (this case)
the seven placements (sprinkled toward the פרוכת)
are essential; leaving them out ruins the service
the four placements (on the corners of the inner מזבח)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two sets: the seven are sprinkled toward the פרוכת, and the four are placed on the inner מזבח. Both belong to the same offering.

phrases.english: I only have the seven placements,
which are essential in every place;
phrases.notes: The seven sprinklings are always essential, so it is easy to say the rule covers them.

phrases.english: from where [do we know] the four placements?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the lesson of step 17 to the seven sprinklings and asks about the four placements.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the four placements on the inner מזבח are also essential.

steps.title: The words 'so shall he do' cover the four placements
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers from the words 'כן יעשה' that the four placements are also essential.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'So shall he do.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers step 18's question by pointing to the words 'כן יעשה' in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'כן' means 'exactly so'. These words tell us the four placements must be done just as commanded, so missing one also ruins the service. Now both sets of placements are essential.

keyTerms.meaning: the verse teaches / says
so shall he do (exactly this way)

steps.whatToRemember: For the פר העלם דבר, all of the placements are essential: the seven from 'ועשה כאשר עשה' and the four from 'כן יעשה'.

phrases.english: The verse states: "So shall he do."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'כן יעשה' teach that the four placements are essential too.

steps.title: 'With the bull' refers to the פר יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא moves to the next word of the פסוק, 'לפר', and says it refers to the פר יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'With the bull': this is the bull of יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא starts reading the next word in the פסוק, 'לפר'. It says the word points to the פר יום הכפורים, which sets up the next part of the derivation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the ברייתא is not looking at the פר העלם דבר alone. It reads 'לפר' as bringing another bull, the פר יום הכפורים, into the discussion. What exactly it learns from this comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: with the bull (a word in the פסוק)
the bull offered by the כהן גדול on יום כיפור

phrases.english: "With the bull" – this is the bull of Yom Kippur,
phrases.notes: From ויקרא 4:20, 'ועשה לפר'. The ברייתא reads this word as pointing to a different bull.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's word-by-word reading of the same פסוק, now on the word 'לפר'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word 'לפר' refers to the פר יום הכפורים.
